619059630d1f.text: AI Is Getting Good at Math. Here’s Why.. In May, an internal model at OpenAI found a counterexample to Erdős's unit distance conjecture . Open since 1946. Many experts had tried to prove it. OpenAI found a counterexample instead. A month later, OpenAI published a proof of the Cycle Double Cover (CDC) problem , then solutions to ten more open problems by July. And a proof of Navier Stokes in September. Anthropic published a formalization of the fermat's last theorem , and advanced bounds on Reimann's hypothesis . The models are suddenly good at math. 5c33d37c37b5.text: Claude Mods: Flipping the Harness Inside Out. For the last few weeks I’ve used Claude Mods to mold Claude Code to my AI engineering workflow. Claude Code is great out of the box, but every engineering workflow is different. Claude Mods let you make Claude Code yours, in the way you want to pay attention. The “paying attention” part is now the most important thing. In a recent Latent Space post, The Evolution of the Agent Harness , I argued that as models absorb more of the harness into their weights, the part that’s left faces the human. It becomes the Attention Interface : the layer that decides when the agent interrupts you, what it shows you, and which decisions it needs you to make.…

debates.title: Open‑weight models challenge closed AI dominance
debates.summary: Open‑weight releases like Kimi 3.1 Pro are narrowing the performance gap with closed‑source leaders, but their mixed reception raises adoption and security questions. The debate centers on whether open models will reshape the frontier AI landscape or introduce new risks.

debates.title: AI models raise new cybersecurity and covert channel fears
debates.summary: Recent findings suggest AI can exploit hardware side‑channels and discover software vulnerabilities, prompting alarm over covert communication and cyber‑risk amplification. Experts debate how realistic these threats are and what safeguards are needed.

debates.title: Governments grapple with regulation of frontier AI models
debates.summary: Both the United States and China are moving toward pre‑approval regimes for frontier AI models, intensifying geopolitical competition and raising questions about export controls. The discussion also touches on how labs might leverage internal‑model advantages in regulated sectors.
